title: A personalized approach using hypoxia resolution to guide curative-intent radiation dose reduction to 30 Gy: A novel de-escalation paradigm for HPV-associated oropharynx cancers
text:
The concept of de-escalation to 30Gy (“low risk”) from standard 70Gy (“high risk”), based on week 2 intra-
treatment 18F-FMISO PET response (negative, 30Gy versus positive, 70Gy) for early-stage (T0-2/N1-2c) human
papillomavirus-related oropharyngeal carcinoma (HPV+ OPC), can be extended to advanced-stage (T3-4/N3)
patients. For those patients who do not have access to 18F-FMISO PET, alternative imaging biomarkers
predicting a negative week 2 FMISO PET synergized with week 2 ctDNA can also be used to select early-stage
HPV+ OPC patients for 30Gy de-escalation. Lastly, our novel advanced machine learning model can select
those patients who did not quality for 30Gy (FMISO positive) as having an “intermediate risk” disease, of which
de-escalation to 46Gy can be done to further reduce toxicity without compromising locoregional control versus
the standard 70Gy.

title: Mni Sota Center for Climate Change and Health
text:
Overall
The Mni Sota Center for Climate Change and Health will build multidisciplinary research capacity related to
climate change and health as experienced by American Indian and rural communities through the innovative
use of data resources and authentic engagement with communities. The goal of the Mni Sota (the Dakota word
for ‘where the waters reflect the sky’) center is to be a leading research center that will characterize health
impacts related to climate change and translate findings to create practical and actionable measures for
climate change adaptation with a specific focus on American Indian and rural communities.

title: ROLE OF PERIPHERAL IMMUNE-DERIVED MMP8 IN STRESS SUSCEPTIBILITY
text:
Psychosocial stress can profoundly impact bi-directional communication between the immune system and brain.
Here, we propose to study how stress mobilizes the innate immune system to increase blood brain barrier
permeability and promote deficits in both social and non-social reward/reinforcement by directly regulating
neuronal activity in brain reward regions such as the nucleus accumbens.

title: Retinoid Metabolism in the Adult Heart and Heart Failure
text:
We have discovered all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA), a metabolite of Vitamin A and master gene-switch that
controls many genes that are important to heart function, declines in patients with one type of human heart failure
(HF) as well as an animal model. We want to understand three things about ATRA and HF: 1. What enzymes
metabolize Vitamin A to ATRA in heart muscle cells? 2. How does low ATRA alter heart function? 3. How
pervasive is low ATRA across different types HF?

title: Gut Microbiome and Cancer Immunotherapy Outcomes in Advanced Renal Cell Carcinoma
text:
Immunotherapy is a new standard-of-care option for the first-line treatment of intermediate-risk or poor-risk
patients with advanced kidney cancer. However, the immunotherapy outcomes are mixed, with some patients
achieving complete remissions, and others having no benefit at all. The purpose of this study is to identify and
confirm microbiome profiles and bacterial functional pathways associated with cancer immunotherapy
response, adverse events, and progression-free survival among patients with advanced kidney cancer.

title: Chronobiological Basis of Depression during the Menopause Transition
text:
The purpose of this study is to investigate the biological basis of mood, sleep and energy (activity)
disturbances in women undergoing the menopausal transition, examine whether disruption in circadian
rhythms measured by melatonin underlies these disturbances, and determine whether critically-timed sleep
and light treatments administered in home environments can correct the biological rhythm dysregulation, and
thereby improve mood, sleep and activity, enhancing health and well-being and preventing further dysfunction
and disability.

title: Unraveling Metastasis Drivers in Small Cell Lung Cancer via Human Pluripotent Stem Cell-Based Approach
text:
Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is among the deadliest malignancies, known for its high metastatic
potential, yet the mechanisms driving its spread remain unclear. Our project uses innovative
methods, including human pluripotent stem cell-derived models, patient-derived xenografts (PDX),
and advanced sequencing technologies, to explore the metastatic process of SCLC. By
generating and studying mutated pulmonary neuroendocrine cells (PNECs), which mimic the
progression of SCLC from initiation, progression to metastasis, we aim to uncover the cellular and
molecular mechanisms underlying the disease's aggressive behavior, potentially leading to new
strategies in diagnosis and treatment.

title: Regulatory RNA in Hypertension and Renal Injury
text:
Hypertension is a leading risk factor for disease burden worldwide and one of the major causes of chronic
kidney disease and end-stage renal disease. The proposed project aims to elucidate a new dimension of
complexity in the development of hypertension and renal injury that involves novel cell type-specific mechanisms.

title: AAV9fyhr gene replacement therapy for PDHA1 deficiency in the E75A mouse model
text:
Primary Pyruvate Dehydrogenase Complex Deficiency (PDCD) is a rare but severe mitochondrial disorder,
with the majority of cases caused by mutations in the PDHA1 gene. Currently, there is no curative therapy for
PDHA1 deficiency, and prognosis remains extremely poor with death occurring in approximately 90% of affected
individuals before the age of four. We propose to use the novel AAV9fyhr vector to deliver the PDHA1 gene to
the central nervous system of a newly developed and characterized E75A mouse model of PDHA1 deficiency
and evaluate the efficacy and safety of the AAV9fyhr/PDHA1 vector, with the ultimate long-term goal to translate
this gene therapy approach into a first-in-human clinical trial for patients with PDHA1 deficiency.

title: Development of a Targetable Transposase Platform for Precision Gene Integration in Human Cells
text:
This project aims to develop a highly specific and efficient gene therapy platform using the piggyBac transposase
to enable precise insertion of large DNA fragments at specific genomic sites. By optimizing the piggyBac
transposase through rational design and directed evolution, this research will address the limitations of current
gene-editing technologies. The outcomes of this project will provide safer and more effective therapies for genetic
diseases by minimizing off-target effects and enhancing the precision of gene delivery.

title: Modulation of cytomegalovirus replication by the viral temperance factor RL13
text:
How and why the viral temperance factor RL13 restricts cytomegalovirus replication remains unknown. The
proposed studies will determine the molecular interactions and mechanisms that mediate the repressive effects
of RL13 and modulate RL13 expression. These results will be among the first to elucidate the mechanisms
whereby certain viral proteins restrict, rather than enhance, viral replication and spread.

title: Neurobiology for Lac-Phe Hypophagia
text:
We recently identified a lactate-derived metabolite called N-lactoyl-phenylalanine (“Lac-Phe”) as the most
significantly elevated metabolite in blood plasma after an intense exercise bout, which can robustly reduce food
intake and body weight in obese mice. The proposed experiments will follow upon these observations to reveal
the neurobiological basis for Lac-Phe hypophagia, which may identify Lac-Phe and the associated pathways as
targets for weight management.

title: A Novel Target in The Tumor Myeloid Compartment for Hepatocellular Carcinoma
text:
PROJECT 3: NARRATIVE
This project addresses a novel innate pattern recognition receptor (i.e., SRA/CD204) in the tumor
microenvironment that can impede immune surveillance and promote therapeutic resistance of hepatocellular
carcinoma (HCC). By gaining an in-depth understanding of the underlying mechanism of SRA function in these
processes and successfully testing blocking antibodies targeting this receptor in preclinical models, we can
significantly advance the current treatment options for HCC.

title: Regulation of generation and functions of intermediate progenitors
text:
Mechanisms that amplify the generation of intermediate progenitors boosts stem cell output in producing
differentiated cells without increasing the frequency of stem cell division thereby safeguarding the long-term
health of stem cells. However, not all stem cells display this amplification mechanism in the physiological context,
and it is unclear how this capacity can be activated to increase the production of differentiated cells on demand.
Our proposal will investigate the mechanisms that control the amplification of intermediate progenitors and how
stem cell-specific functions can be properly regulated in general to ensure normal brain development and to
prevent brain tumor formation.

title: Unraveling Human T Follicular Helper Cell Development
text:
Human T follicular helper cells function by providing essential support to B cells in draining lymph nodes allowing
those B cells to produce highly effective neutralizing antibodies following vaccination or infection. The dynamics
of human antigen-specific T follicular helper cell development, maturation and function are not well-understood.
The work we propose will fill this knowledge gap and lead to a deeper understanding of the impact of human T
follicular helper cell maturation on function in the setting of a very efficacious human lipid nanoparticle mRNA
vaccine platform.

title: Ultrasensitive Env Detection Assay for Broadly Neutralizing Antibody Screening
text:
There is a clear association between the neutralization sensitivity of virus and how effective bNAbs are in
suppressing virus replication during clinical trials; however, there are two main obstacles that limit the use of this
assay: length of assay time and difficulty in obtaining the correct samples to test. We propose an ultra-sensitive
Env binding assay whose results will correlate to neutralization assay results but will take hours, and that can
directly measure translationally competent virus directly in cells lysates, increasing the sampling depth. Our multi-
disciplinary team has all the expertise necessary to achieve these aims that, when completed, result in an ultra-
sensitive binding assay for Env protein to screen clinical trial participants that is time efficient, accurate and
qualified.

title: A Multimethod Examination of Individual and Environmental Contributors to Cannabis Use and Related Problems
text: The proposed project tests a cascading model that examines chronic stress, reactivity to acute stressors, and cannabis cognitions, inside the laboratory and in the natural environment, as contributors to cannabis use and problems. Results of the project will inform just-in-time mobile health intervention efforts by identifying modifiable and proximal treatment targets and will ultimately lead to a reduction in the negative impact of heavy cannabis use and cannabis use disorder.

title: Molecular Mechanisms of Tubulin Polymerization Promoting Protein in Mitochondrial Function and Neuronal Survival
text:
Neurodegenerative diseases, including Parkinson’s disease (PD), Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias
(AD/ADRD), are among the fastest growing diseases afflicting millions of people worldwide with tremendous
economic and societal burdens. A highly conserved and less understood family of human Tubulin
Polymerization Promoting Proteins (TPPP) is implicated in PD and related disorders. Using a model system
and postmortem human brains of healthy individuals and PD patients, this proposal seeks to elucidate novel
mitochondrial mechanisms underlying TPPP functions in promoting neuronal survival and gain insights into
disease pathogenesis.

title: Continuous Neurogenesis in the Mammalian Hippocampus
text:
Adult hippocampal neurogenesis reflects the continuous preservation of neural stem cells in the mature brain.
Using both animal and human models, understanding the origin and function of these neural stem cells can
reveal new targets to enhance plasticity and prevent dysregulation due to developmental disorders, neural
injury or degeneration.

title: Predoctoral Training Program in Human Genetics
text:
Advances in human genetics and genomics continue at an astounding rate and increasingly they are being
integrated into medical practice. The Johns Hopkins Predoctoral Training Program in Human Genetics (HG)
aims to educate highly motivated and capable students with the knowledge and experimental tools that will
enable them to answer important questions at the interface between genetics and medicine. Ultimately, our
trainees will be the leaders in delivering the promise of genetics to human health.
